requirement: The review prompt MUST direct the reviewer never to rename or move a committed requirement, and to raise a wrong name as a design question instead. When the reviewer splits a committed requirement, the prompt MUST direct it to keep the requirement's full name on the core obligation, to name the parts `<name>.<part>`, and to list every new name.
rationale:
The requirement has two clauses, and the review prompt and test cover both.

**Implementation:** `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/references/review-prompt.md` carries the {impl} reference. In the "Mechanical changes" section it says: "Never rename or move a committed requirement; if its name is wrong, raise it as a design question. When you split one, keep its full name on the core obligation and name the parts `<name>.<part>`, so existing references still resolve. List every new name." That maps to the obligations as follows:
- Never rename or move a committed requirement: "Never rename or move a committed requirement".
- Raise a wrong name as a design question: "if its name is wrong, raise it as a design question".
- Keep the full name on the core obligation when splitting: "keep its full name on the core obligation".
- Name the parts `<name>.<part>`: "name the parts `<name>.<part>`".
- List every new name: "List every new name."

The added clause "so existing references still resolve" gives a reason and does not add unspecified behavior.

**Test:** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_review_prompt_never_renames_and_names_split_parts]` carries the {test} reference. It takes the prompt text between "**Mechanical changes:**" and "**Design questions:**" (via `review_prompt_between`) and uses `assert_text` to require three phrases. They cover never renaming or moving and raising a wrong name as a design question, keeping the full name and naming the parts `<name>.<part>`, and listing every new name. Each obligation has an assertion that would fail if the wording were removed.

No gaps found.
